broad_instruction_source: Control Issue #375's real mid-cycle comment (issuecomment-5541631991, posted 2026-09-04T14:08:49Z), used per this unit's own Worker Unit Contract as the representative broad instruction: "A fresh controller resumes with `work on #375`: check PR #376 Stage 1 status with `node tools/review-watch/stage1-gate.mjs ...` (or `poll.mjs` if still pending). On a genuine response, verify/fix findings if any, then merge per docs/bounded-review-cycle.md's composed pre-merge gate, open the Stage 2 audit issue, trigger it, and end."
why_this_is_a_genuine_negative_control: This sentence, read as prose, authorizes a controller to: (1) check Stage 1 status, (2) verify/fix findings, (3) merge, (4) open the Stage 2 issue, (5) trigger it, and (6) end -- i.e. it spans Watched Lifecycle Breakpoints 2 and 3 in one continuation if a controller followed it literally start to finish.
verdict: Regardless of what #375's own prose says a fresh controller may do next, the corrected mechanism -- consulted at the exact real PR/head that prose refers to -- returns exactly one verdict carrying a literal stopAfter:true field. The verdict's own defined action (per next-review-transition-gate.mjs's module comment) is 'perform the merge and open+trigger the Stage 2 Audit Issue; once that reference is durable, this verdict's job is done -- the gate does not itself continue on to check Stage 2.' A controller consulting this gate (rather than reasoning freely from #375's prose) structurally cannot continue past the merge+trigger action in the same reasoning context, because the gate itself supplies no further instruction to continue on -- it has already stopped.
second_negative_control_confirmation: docs/operating-model.md (397-A's documentation unit, already shipped on `feature/397-transition-gates` at commit 1481ca3, verified present by direct grep during this unit's own work) additionally retires prose as dispatch authority directly, quoting this exact #375 sentence by name: 'A control Issue's free-text "Next authorized transition" sentence remains useful for a founder skimming the issue, but it is never itself dispatch authority once this gate exists. #375's mid-cycle comment -- "check PR #376 Stage 1 status ... verify/fix findings if any, then merge ... open the Stage 2 audit issue, trigger it, and end" -- reads as a correct-looking sequence, and nothing mechanically stopped a controller from executing all of it in one reasoning context; that is the actual defect this section closes ... The authoritative source of "what happens next" for a post-PR control Issue is this gate's live verdict, never a prose paragraph, no matter how correct each individual step in it sounds.' This is a second, independent form of the same guard -- the governing contract itself, not only the tool's behavior.
observation: The mechanism, not reviewer discipline, is what makes the multi-breakpoint instruction inert: the gate's own JSON output is the only thing a corrected controller consults, and that output structurally contains one verdict and nothing past it -- exactly what scenario 6 requires to demonstrate.
